meanings: circles (as in a field of work)

components.note: 田 (field) — recalls the original idea of a boundary line between farm plots
介 (jiè) gives the sound — it matches 界's reading exactly

example.hanzi: 这条河是两个省的分界。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé shì liǎng gè shěng de fēnjiè.
example.english: This river is the boundary between the two provinces.
example.fact: 界 rarely stands alone; it works as a suffix meaning 'a field or circle of people', as in 娱乐界 (the entertainment world) or 教育界 (educational circles), and it is also the second half of 世界 'world'.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — searching is done by hand, rummaging through things
叟 (sǒu) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá sōu le tā de fángjiān.
example.english: The police searched his room.
example.fact: On its own 搜 is mostly used for physical searches or in the casual internet sense, as in 搜一下 'look it up'; in formal writing it usually appears in compounds like 搜索 (search) and 搜查 (search a place).

components.note: This is the simplified form of 齊, and its shape no longer shows a clear picture of why it means 'even, neat'; learn it as a single unit.

example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu dào qí le.
example.english: Everyone has arrived.
example.fact: 齐 often follows a verb as a result complement meaning 'completely, all present', as in 到齐 or 备齐 (get everything ready). It is also the name of an ancient state in what is now Shandong, so you will see it in 齐国 and as a surname.

components.note: 木 (wood) — the meaning side, hinting at the character's origin in wooden objects
交 (jiāo) gives the sound — the final -iao is shared with xiào

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài xiàoménkǒu jiànmiàn.
example.english: We'll meet at the school gate.
example.fact: Meaning 'school', 校 appears in compounds like 学校, 校长 (principal) and 校园 (campus). The same character read jiào means 'to proofread', as in 校对, so check the reading when you meet it.

components.note: 兹 is built from two 幺 (tiny threads) under a cap; its parts do not give a helpful clue to the meaning, so it is best learned as a unit.

example.pinyin: Cí zhèngmíng tā shì běn xiào xuésheng.
example.english: This is to certify that he is a student of this school.
example.fact: 兹 is a formal, officialese word for 'this/now', most often seen in the opening of notices and certificates such as 兹证明 or 兹通知 ('hereby'). It is not used in speech.

excludeSuggestion: Formal/classical word that appears almost only in official notices and certificates; learners rarely need it early.

components.note: 十 (ten) — suggests something passed down through many generations
口 (mouth) — old sayings and stories handed down by word of mouth

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí zuò hěn gǔ de chéngshì.
example.english: This is a very ancient city.
example.fact: 古 means 'of ancient times' and is used in compounds like 古代 and 古老, whereas 老 describes ordinary age. So an old building you simply find worn is 老房子, but a historic one is a 古建筑.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — sowing seeds is done by hand
番 (fān) is the second part and also hints at the sound of 播

example.pinyin: Diànshìtái zhèngzài bō xīnwén.
example.english: The TV station is broadcasting the news.
example.fact: The original sense is 'to sow seeds', and the idea of scattering carried over to broadcasting. Today 播 is everywhere in media words: 播放 (play), 广播 (radio) and 直播 (livestream).

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a closed outline fits the idea of a round shape
员 (yuán) gives the sound — it matches 圆 exactly

example.pinyin: Jīnwǎn de yuèliang yòu dà yòu yuán.
example.english: Tonight the moon is big and round.
example.fact: Roundness symbolises completeness in Chinese culture, which is why 团圆 means a family reunion and the round full moon of Mid-Autumn is tied to togetherness. 圆 is also the formal way to write the currency unit 元 in some contexts.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — drills and borers are metal tools
占 (zhàn) gives a rough sound — the initial and final are close to zuān

example.pinyin: Lǎoshǔ zuān jìn le dòng lǐ.
example.english: The mouse crept into the hole.
example.fact: 钻 has two readings: zuān is the verb 'to drill or squeeze into', while zuàn is the noun 'a drill, a diamond' as in 钻石. Don't mix them up: 钻进 (zuānjìn) means 'to burrow into'.

components.note: 广 (wide shelter) — a large covered building
廷 (tíng) is the court; it also gives the sound

example.pinyin: Háizimen zài tíngyuàn lǐ wán.
example.english: The children are playing in the courtyard.
example.fact: 庭 started as a courtyard or palace hall, and the sense of 'court' extended to the family (家庭) and to a court of law (法庭). It is seldom a free-standing word and mostly appears in such compounds.

components.note: 页 (head) — the head turning to go along with something; 页 is the meaning part
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound clue, though its flowing-river image also fits 'going smoothly'

example.pinyin: Jīntiān de gōngzuò hěn shùn.
example.english: Work went smoothly today.
example.fact: 顺 turns up in many greetings and set phrases, such as 一路顺风 ('smooth sailing') and 顺便 ('by the way, while you're at it'). As a verb, 顺着 means 'along', as in 顺着这条路走.

components.note: 攵 (tapping hand) — the action part, suggesting the movement of scattering something

example.hanzi: 会议结束了，大家都散了。
example.pinyin: Huìyì jiéshù le, dàjiā dōu sàn le.
example.english: The meeting is over and everyone has dispersed.
example.fact: 散 has two readings: sàn is the verb 'to scatter or break up', as in 散步 'go for a stroll', while sǎn means 'loose, in pieces', as in 散装 (sold loose) or 散文 (prose).

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings held in the heart or chest
不 (bù) is only a rough sound clue for 怀 huái

example.pinyin: Tā huáizhe mèngxiǎng lái dào Běijīng.
example.english: She came to Beijing cherishing a dream.
example.fact: 怀 as a verb means 'to carry in one's chest or heart', so it links both the physical (怀孕, pregnant) and the emotional (怀念, to long for someone gone). It goes with abstract nouns such as 怀着希望 'full of hope'.

components.note: 壴 (zhù) — an old drum, as in celebration
口 (mouth) — singing and laughing

example.pinyin: Gōngxǐ nǐ kǎo shàng le dàxué!
example.english: Congratulations on getting into university!
example.fact: 喜 is the root of 喜欢 'to like' and 恭喜 'congratulations', and a doubled form 囍 is a classic wedding decoration. As a free word it is mostly set-phrase, as in 喜事 'a happy event' and 报喜 'to announce good news'.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person leaning or resting
木 (tree) — a tree to lean against, picturing a rest

example.hanzi: 工作了一天，他想休息一下。
example.pinyin: Gōngzuò le yì tiān, tā xiǎng xiūxi yíxià.
example.english: After working all day, he wants to rest a bit.
example.fact: 休 is rarely used alone for 'rest' in modern speech: you normally say 休息 or 休假 (take leave). It also appears in the stern phrase 休想, 'don't even think about it'.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — a movement radical, relating to the idea of stopping or pausing
豆 (dòu) gives the sound — it matches 逗 exactly

example.hanzi: 他讲的笑话把大家都逗笑了。
example.pinyin: Tā jiǎng de xiàohua bǎ dàjiā dōu dòu xiào le.
example.english: The joke he told made everyone laugh.
example.fact: 逗 also means 'a pause', which is why the comma is 逗号. As a verb it is common in 逗笑 'to make someone laugh' and 逗小孩 'to play with a child', and colloquially 你真逗 means 'you're hilarious'.

components.note: 王 (jade) — an old form of the jade radical
见 (jiàn) — to see; also hints at the sound

example.pinyin: Tā tūrán chūxiàn zài ménkǒu.
example.english: He suddenly appeared at the door.
example.fact: 现 almost always appears in compounds: 现在 (now), 出现 (appear), 现金 (cash). Colloquially it can mean 'on the spot', as in 现做现吃 ('cook it and eat it fresh').

components.note: 心 (heart) — worry weighing on the heart
串 (chuàn) is a loose sound clue for huàn

example.pinyin: Tā huàn le zhòng gǎnmào.
example.english: He came down with a bad cold.
example.fact: 患 is a formal verb for 'to suffer from' a disease, and it sits in 患者 'patient' and 患病 'to fall ill'. In everyday talk people say 得了 for catching a cold, so 患 sounds medical or written.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — a symbol of good fortune and gentleness
口 (mouth) — speaking kindly

example.hanzi: 她是一个心地善良的人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè xīndì shànliáng de rén.
example.english: She is a kind-hearted person.
example.fact: 善 is the root of 善良 (kind), 友善 (friendly) and 善于 + verb, 'to be good at (doing)', which is a useful pattern for describing skills. 善 as a lone noun is tied to the moral idea of 'goodness', as in 善恶 'good and evil'.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — silk threads wrapping around something
㢆 gives the sound — it is a rare character, close to chán

example.pinyin: Xiǎohái chán zhe māma yào wánjù.
example.english: The child keeps pestering mom for a toy.
example.fact: 缠 shows up in both the literal (a vine 缠 around a tree) and the figurative: someone who 'clings and pesters' you is 缠着你, and a lingering illness or problem is 缠身. Compare 纠缠 'to entangle'.

components.note: A pictograph of a sheep or goat's head seen from the front, showing the two curved horns.

example.pinyin: Shān shàng yǒu hěn duō yáng.
example.english: There are many sheep on the mountain.
example.fact: Chinese uses 羊 for both sheep and goats; to be precise you say 绵羊 (sheep) or 山羊 (goat). Its measure word is 只 or 头, and 羊 is the eighth animal of the Chinese zodiac.

components.note: 亦 (yì) forms the top; in this simplified form it offers no clear link to the meaning
虫 (insect) — an old tag used for southern peoples, giving the original sense 'barbarian'

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de cài mán hǎochī de.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is quite tasty.
example.fact: As an adverb, 蛮 is a colloquial 'quite, rather', used as 蛮 + adjective + 的, especially in the south: 蛮好的, 蛮贵的. The original 'barbarian' sense survives in words like 野蛮 and is considered rude.

components.note: 工 (work) — skilled craftsmanship
丂 (kǎo) gives the sound — close to qiǎo

example.pinyin: Zhēn qiǎo, wǒmen yòu jiànmiàn le.
example.english: What a coincidence, we meet again.
example.fact: 巧 covers both 'skill' (灵巧 nimble) and 'coincidence', as in 真巧! ('what a coincidence!') and 碰巧 ('happen to'). Look out: in 巧克力 (chocolate) it only supplies the sound qiǎo.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — shaking is a hand action
䍃 (yáo) gives the sound — it matches 摇 exactly

example.pinyin: Tā yáoyao tóu, shuō bù zhīdào.
example.english: He shook his head and said he didn't know.
example.fact: 摇头 (shake the head) signals 'no' and 点头 (nod) signals 'yes', just as in English. 摇 also names rock music as 摇滚, and 摇篮 means a cradle.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — slow cooking over a flame
敖 (áo) gives the sound — it matches 熬 exactly

example.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng áo zhōu.
example.english: Mom is cooking congee in the kitchen.
example.fact: 熬 has the sense 'to cook slowly' (熬汤, 熬粥) and 'to endure a hardship', and it is the second half of 熬夜, 'to stay up late'. The same character read āo is a less common dialect cooking word, so áo is the one to learn.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — meeting someone on the road
禺 (yù) gives the sound — a close match to yù

example.hanzi: 我在路上遇到了老同学。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài lù shàng yùdào le lǎo tóngxué.
example.english: I ran into an old classmate on the road.
example.fact: 遇 seldom stands alone: 遇到 and 遇见 mean 'to run into', while 遇 implies an unplanned meeting. For problems you can also say 遇到困难 ('to run into difficulty').

meanings: measure word for streams, scents, forces

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — a body part, the thigh
殳 (shū) is a loose sound clue for gǔ

example.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ piāolái yì gǔ xiāngwèi.
example.english: A whiff of something delicious drifted from the kitchen.
example.fact: As a measure word 股 counts things that flow or rise: 一股香味 (a scent), 一股力量 (a surge of strength). It also means 'share', which is why 股票 are stocks and 股东 are shareholders.

components.note: 开 (kāi) — this left part contributes little direct meaning
彡 (strokes) — often marks patterns or appearances

example.pinyin: Zhège hézi shì yuánxíng de.
example.english: This box is round-shaped.
example.fact: 形 attaches to shape words: 圆形 (circle), 方形 (square), 形状 (shape). In grammar 形容词 is the 'adjective', literally a word that 'describes form'.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — thinness tied to illness in older times
叟 (sǒu) gives the sound — similar to shòu

example.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn shòu le hěn duō.
example.english: He has lost a lot of weight recently.
example.fact: 瘦 contrasts with 胖 for people and with 肥 for meat (瘦肉 lean meat vs 肥肉 fatty meat). With clothes it means 'tight-fitting': 这件衣服太瘦了.

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — a plant bud
雷 (léi) gives the sound — only the tone differs

example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ de huālěi kuài kāi le.
example.english: The flower buds in the garden are about to open.
example.fact: 蕾 is rarely used on its own; it appears in 花蕾 or 蓓蕾 (bud), and in 味蕾, the word for 'taste buds' on the tongue. 蓓蕾 is also used figuratively for young talent.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a household or an official's hall
辛 (xīn) — a harsh tool or hardship; here a sharp blade

example.hanzi: 过年的时候，他们宰了一只羊。
example.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou, tāmen zǎi le yì zhī yáng.
example.english: At New Year they slaughtered a sheep.
example.fact: 宰 is the plain verb for slaughtering animals, and slangily it means 'to fleece' a customer: 被宰了 'I got ripped off'. It also appears in 宰相, the ancient 'chancellor' title.

components.note: 戎 (weapons) — violence and arms, as in a robber
贝 (bèi) is the listed sound part, though the match to zéi is weak; its 'valuables' meaning also fits

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhuā dào le nàge zéi.
example.english: The police caught that thief.
example.fact: 贼 means 'thief' (a petty thief is more commonly called 小偷 in speech), but northern speakers also use it as a vivid adverb: 贼冷 is 'freezing cold'. A common idiom, 贼喊捉贼, means 'a thief crying thief'.

components.note: 木 (wood) — wooden shelves or frames that hold documents
当 (dāng) gives the sound — a close match to dàng

example.hanzi: 我把旧档案放进了柜子里。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ jiù dàng'àn fàng jìn le guìzi lǐ.
example.english: I put the old files into the cabinet.
example.fact: 档 sits in 档案 (files, records), and in grade words like 高档 (high-end) and 低档 (low-end). It also names a time slot, as in 档期 (release window), and in Taiwan it is how the gears of a car are counted.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the meaning side; its tie to the number is by convention
乙 (yǐ) gives the sound — same syllable, different tone

example.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒu shí jǐ yì rénkǒu.
example.english: China has over a billion people.
example.fact: 亿 means 100 million, not a billion, because Chinese groups big numbers by 万 (10,000). So 十亿 is a billion and 一百亿 is ten billion; always convert to 万 and 亿 when reading large figures.

components.note: Its shape (a 心 with a stroke across it) is not a reliable guide to the meaning 'must'; treat the whole as one unit.

example.pinyin: Nǐ búbì zhème zháojí.
example.english: You don't need to be in such a hurry.
example.fact: 必 is mostly a formal adverb: 必须 (must), 必然 (inevitable) and 不必 ('need not') are the most common. 必 can also appear as 未必 'not necessarily', a handy phrase for politely disagreeing.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a building
吕 (lǚ) is only a loose sound clue; its shape shows linked rooms

example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān qù Gùgōng.
example.english: We're going to the Forbidden City tomorrow.
example.fact: 宫 refers to a palace, especially an imperial one, so the Beijing Forbidden City is 故宫 ('former palace'). It also names the 子宫 (uterus) and Taoist temples, and is the first note of the traditional five-note scale.

components.note: 里 (a unit of length) — measuring is about a unit
旦 (dàn) gives a rough sound clue

example.pinyin: Hùshi gěi wǒ liáng le tǐwēn.
example.english: The nurse took my temperature.
example.fact: The character 量 has two readings: liáng is the verb 'to measure', as in 量体温 or 量身高, while liàng is the noun 'amount, capacity', as in 数量 and 力量. They are different words with the same spelling.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — a vegetable or plant
罗 (luó) gives the sound — it matches 萝 exactly

example.pinyin: Māma zài dùn luóbo tāng.
example.english: Mom is stewing radish soup.
example.fact: 萝 is nearly always followed by 卜 as 萝卜 (radish); 胡萝卜 is carrot, literally 'foreign radish'. The syllable 卜 in 萝卜 is read bo in neutral tone, not bǔ.

excludeSuggestion: Bound character: it almost only occurs in 萝卜 (radish) and similar plant names.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person
子 (zǐ) — a child; also hints at the sound

example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yì tiáo niúzǎikù.
example.english: He is wearing a pair of jeans.
example.fact: 仔 is used for 'young' creatures in southern speech (猪仔 piglet) and Cantonese-influenced terms such as 靓仔. In Mandarin it appears most in 牛仔裤 (jeans), literally 'cowboy pants', and as zǐ in 仔细 'careful'.

excludeSuggestion: Mainly occurs in compounds like 牛仔 and 仔细 (where it is read zǐ); rarely a standalone word.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — sewing with thread
逢 (féng) gives the sound — it matches 缝 exactly

example.pinyin: Māma zài féng yīfu.
example.english: Mom is sewing clothes.
example.fact: 缝 has two readings: féng is the verb 'to sew' (缝衣服), while fèng is the noun 'a gap or seam', as in 门缝 (a door crack) and 缝隙. Context usually makes it clear which one you want.

components.note: 舌 (tongue) — licking is done with the tongue
忝 (tiǎn) gives the sound — it matches 舔 exactly

example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu tiǎn le tiǎn wǒ de shǒu.
example.english: The puppy licked my hand.
example.fact: 舔 is the ordinary verb for licking, as with 舔手指 (lick one's fingers). On the internet, 舔狗 ('licking dog') became slang for someone who fawns over a person without being loved back.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — a hanging cloth, a curtain
莫 (mò) gives the sound — close to mù

example.pinyin: Dà mù mànmàn de lākāi le.
example.english: The big curtain slowly opened.
example.fact: 幕 means a curtain, and in compounds: 银幕 (cinema screen), 字幕 (subtitles) and 夜幕 (the 'curtain' of night). It is also the measure word for acts in a play: 第一幕 is Act One.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — the heart racing in fright
京 (jīng) gives the sound — it matches 惊 exactly

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息，我很吃惊。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, wǒ hěn chījīng.
example.english: I was shocked to hear this news.
example.fact: 惊 lies behind many reaction words: 吃惊 (be shocked), 惊讶 (astonished), 惊喜 (a pleasant surprise) and 惊吓 (a fright). Note that 惊喜 is positive while 惊吓 is not.

components.note: 又 (hand) — the simplified form replaced the old left part, so it adds no direct meaning
力 (strength) — the effort of encouraging someone

example.pinyin: Péngyou quàn wǒ duō xiūxi.
example.english: My friend urged me to get more rest.
example.fact: 劝 means to try to convince someone, without implying success: 我劝了他，但他不听 ('I advised him, but he didn't listen'). To say you succeeded in persuading, use 说服.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a female relative
未 (wèi) gives the sound — similar to mèi

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí gè mèimei.
example.english: I have a younger sister.
example.fact: 妹 refers to a younger sister, and is almost always doubled as 妹妹 or used in 姐妹 (sisters). Chinese does not have a generic word for 'sister': you must choose 姐姐 (older) or 妹妹 (younger).

components.note: 夫 (fū) — a grown man, the person in the middle
丷 (two small strokes) — the two people flanking him

example.pinyin: Tā yòng kuàizi jiā le yí kuài ròu.
example.english: He picked up a piece of meat with chopsticks.
example.fact: 夹 pictures a person squeezed between two others, hence 'to clamp or pinch': 夹菜 means to pick up food with chopsticks, and 夹子 is a clip. The word 夹克 for 'jacket' is just a loan from English.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — swallowing happens at the mouth
天 (tiān) gives the sound — close to tūn

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yàopiàn tūn le xiàqù.
example.english: He swallowed the pill.
example.fact: 吞 means to swallow something whole or to gulp, like 吞药. For ordinary throat-swallowing of saliva or food, 咽 is common, and idioms like 狼吞虎咽 ('wolf swallow, tiger gulp') describe wolfing down food.

components.note: 火 (fire) — what is left after a fire; it also suggests the sound

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu yì céng huī.
example.english: There's a layer of dust on the table.
example.fact: 灰 can be ash, dust or the color gray, so 灰色 (gray) is common in daily speech. It also extends to feelings: 灰心 (literally 'ashen heart') means 'to lose heart, be disheartened'.

components.note: 目 (eye) — hiding something from sight
㒼 (mán) is the sound part, written 艹+两 here, reading mán

example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí mánzhe jiārén.
example.english: He has been hiding it from his family.
example.fact: 瞒 takes the person you hide things from as its object: 瞒着我 'behind my back, keeping me in the dark'. A formal synonym is 隐瞒 (to conceal).

components.note: 足 (foot) — stepping with the foot
沓 (tà) gives the sound — it matches 踏 exactly

example.pinyin: Tā yì jiǎo tà jìn le shuǐ lǐ.
example.english: He stepped right into the water.
example.fact: 踏 is the written word for stepping; speech prefers 踩. It forms 踏青 ('tread the green', a spring outing) and 踏实, read tāshi, meaning 'steady' or 'at ease' (a special reading).
